## reading data

```{r}
#load in data files here 
#reading excel files: 
Height_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Seedling Heights")

Moist_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "Soil Moisture")

SPAD_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "SPAD", 
             na = "NA")  #tells it to read NA as missing data 
```

```{r}
#licor raw data 
LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",              
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             n_max = 3,           
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |>  
  unlist() |> 
  unname()  

LICOR_Data_Raw <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx",  
             sheet = "LICOR", 
             skip = 3,   
             col_names = LICOR_Data_Raw_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")


ALL_Licor_NAMES <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             n_max = 3, 
             col_names = FALSE, 
             col_types = "text") |> 
  summarise(across(.fns = paste, collapse = "_")) |> 
  unlist() |> 
  unname()

ALL_Licor <- 
  read_excel("Oak Data Entry MCRS Field Trip.xlsx", 
             sheet = "ALL_Licor_Ignore", 
             skip = 3, 
             col_names = ALL_Licor_NAMES, 
             col_types = "text")

LICOR_Data_Raw <- full_join(LICOR_Data_Raw, ALL_Licor) 
```

## data cleaning

overview on basic data cleaning steps

### LICOR Data Cleaning:

```{r, LICOR CLEANING}

#dropping unecessary columns: 
LICOR1 <- LICOR_Data_Raw |> select(SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD, `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`,  Treatment_NA_NA, `PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1`, `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`)

#renaming colums: 
LICOR2 <- LICOR1 |> rename(date = SYS_Date_YYYYMMDD , 
                           block = `USERDEF_Block Number_NA`, 
                           treatment = Treatment_NA_NA , 
                           conduct = `PORO_gsw_mol+1m-2s-1`, 
                           transpir = `PORO_E_apparent_mmol+1m-2s-1`, 
                           tagnum = `USERDEF_Tag Number_NA`)


#reassign data types: 

#treatment and block: character --> factor 
LICOR3 <- LICOR2 |> mutate(treatment = as.factor(treatment))

#date: charcter --> factor W/ levels 
LICOR3 <- LICOR3 |> mutate(date = as.factor(date), 
                           levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 

#block: character --> factor
LICOR3 <- LICOR3 |> mutate(block = as.factor(block))

#conductance and transpiration: character --> numeric 
LICOR3 <- LICOR3 |> mutate(across
                           (c(conduct, transpir), #select columns
                             as.numeric)) #converting 2 numerical 


glimpse(LICOR3)  #double checking work

#find and get rid block 4.0: 
LICOR4 <- LICOR3 |> filter(block != "4.0")
```

```{r}
#filling in LICOR treatment values: 
LICOR5 <- LICOR4 |> fill(treatment, .direction = "down" )

```

LICOR summary table will go here i guess- make a nice one so it also includes sample sizes

### SPAD cleaning instead:

```{r}
#selecting only columns i want: 
SPAD1 <- SPAD_Data_Raw |> select(Date, Block, Treatment, Tag_Num, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6) 

#rename columns: 
SPAD2 <- SPAD1 |> rename( sdate = Date, 
                            sblock = Block, 
                            streatment = Treatment,
                          stag = Tag_Num) 

#reassign data types:

#block and treatment: character --> factor
SPAD3 <- SPAD2 |> mutate(across
                           (c(sblock, streatment),
                             as.factor))

#date: charcter --> factor with levels 
SPAD3 <- SPAD3 |> mutate(sdate = as.factor(sdate), 
                           levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 


#creating mean across leaves rowwise: 
SPAD4 <- SPAD3 |> rowwise() |> mutate(leaf_mean = mean(
  c(Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6), na.rm = TRUE
)) |> ungroup() 


```

```{r}
#trying to remove tag letters to make it more compatible with LICOR: 
#removing rows full of NA 
SPAD5 <- SPAD4[1:103, ]

#removing A/B/C tags, to help join to LICOR / others 
SPAD6 <- separate(SPAD5, col = stag, into = c("stag", "bs"), sep = 3 )

#selecting only columns I want again: 
SPAD6 <- SPAD6 |> select (sblock, stag, streatment, Leaf1, Leaf2, Leaf3, Leaf4, Leaf5, Leaf6, leaf_mean)
```

### NOT GOING TO USE: Soil Moisture Data Cleaning:

```{r, SOILMOIST CLEANING}

#removing unecessary columns: 
MOIST1 <- Moist_Data_Raw |>  select(Date, Block, Treatment, VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc)

#rename columns: 
MOIST2 <- MOIST1 |> rename( mdate = Date, 
                            mblock = Block, 
                            mtreatment = Treatment, 
)

#reassign data type: 

#date: charcter --> factor with levels 
MOIST3 <- MOIST2 |> mutate(mdate = as.factor(mdate), 
                           levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 

#block and treatment: character --> factor
MOIST3 <- MOIST3 |> mutate(across
                           (c(mblock, mtreatment),
                             as.factor))


#VWC's: character --> numeric 
MOIST3 <- MOIST3 |> mutate(across
                           (c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), #select columns
                             as.numeric)) #converting 2 numerical 

glimpse(MOIST3) #checking work 


# add column with VWC average per row:
MOIST4 <- MOIST3 |> rowwise() |>
  mutate(vwc_mean = mean(
  c(VWC1_perc, VWC2_perc, VWC3_perc), na.rm = TRUE
)) |> ungroup()


#averaging one more time. most blocks and treatments only have 1 observation but this fixes the few that have 2: 
MOIST5 <- MOIST4 |> group_by(mblock, mtreatment) |> 
  mutate(mean_mean = mean(vwc_mean, na.rm=TRUE))
```

soil moisture summary table?

### Sapling Height Data Cleaning:

```{r, HEIGHT CLEANING}

#dropping uneeded rows: 
TALL1 <- Height_Data_Raw |>  select(Date, Block, Tag_Num, Treatment, Sapling_AB_etc, Seedling_Ht_cm, Dead_Alive, Notes)

#rename columns: 
TALL2 <- TALL1 |> rename( tdate = Date, 
                          tblock = Block, 
                          ttreatment = Treatment, 
                          ttag = Tag_Num, 
                          tsap_AB = Sapling_AB_etc, 
                          tht = Seedling_Ht_cm, 
                          dead_alive = Dead_Alive, 
                          notes = Notes
)

#reclassifying data types: 

#block and treatment: character --> factor
TALL3 <- TALL2 |> mutate(across
                         (c(tblock, ttreatment, dead_alive),
                           as.factor))

#date: charcter --> factor with levels 
TALL3 <- TALL3 |> mutate(tdate = as.factor(tdate), 
                           levels(c(2026-10-08, 2026-10-15))) #assigning levels 

glimpse(TALL3) #double checking work 
```


#### Dividing data wet/dry:

```{r, WET/DRY}
#dividing data by wet and dry: 

#LICOR: 
DRYLICOR <- LICOR5 |> filter(
  block == "001" | block =="002"| block =="003" | block =="004")

WETLICOR <- LICOR5 |> filter(
  block =="005" | block =="006" | block =="007" | block =="008"
)

#HEIGHT: 
DRYTALL <- TALL3 |> filter(
  tblock == "001" | tblock =="002"| tblock =="003" | tblock =="004")

WETTALL <- TALL3 |> filter(
  tblock =="005" | tblock =="006" | tblock =="007" | tblock =="008")

#SOIL MOISTURE: 
DRYMOIST <- MOIST5 |>  filter(
  mblock == "001" | mblock =="002"| mblock =="003" | mblock =="004")

WETMOIST <- MOIST5 |> filter(
  mblock =="005" | mblock =="006" | mblock =="007" | mblock =="008")

```

### test area for joining:

```{r}

#creating seed height average, grouping by block, tag, and treatment: 
TESTTALL <- WETTALL |> group_by(ttag, tsap_AB) |> mutate(
  ht_mean = mean(tht))

#replacing OS in height to match OS in LICOR: 
TESTTALL$ttreatment[TESTTALL$ttreatment=="OA"]<- "OS" #why the hell is it OA in this file only. who did this 

#JOINING licor and height data
TEST_HTLICOR <- full_join(WETLICOR, TESTTALL,
                          by = c('block'='tblock', 
                                 'tagnum' = 'ttag',
                                 'treatment' = 'ttreatment')) 

#selecting wnated columns again: 
CLEANJOIN <- TEST_HTLICOR |> select(block, tagnum, treatment, transpir, ht_mean)

#joining moisture to LICOR + height: 
CLEANJOIN2 <- full_join(TEST_HTLICOR, SPAD6, by = 
                          c('block' = 'sblock', 
                            'tagnum' = 'stag', 
                            'treatment' = 'streatment'))

```

## ANOVA:

```{r, ASSUMPTIONS + MODEL}
#checking normality: 
WETLICOR |> ggplot() + aes(x = treatment, y = transpir) + 
  geom_boxplot()

hist(WETLICOR$transpir) #i think its normal,,, 


#setting up model: 
WET_L_MODEL <- lm(transpir ~ treatment + block, data = WETLICOR)
summary(WET_L_MODEL)

#looking at residuals and qqs: 
plot(WET_L_MODEL, which = c(1,2))

#homogeniety of variance: 
bartlett.test(transpir ~ treatment , data = LICORWET) #not homogeneous
WETLICOR |> rstatix::levene_test(transpir ~ treatment)#again, not homogeneous

```

```{r, ANOVA}
#ANOVA test
anova(WET_L_MODEL)
#very significant differences between treatment types, also differences in block?? why is block here
```
